extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners, applicants, and parties to public-use/protest/reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for conducting public-use/on-sale proceedings and for submitting, handling, and petitioning to expunge trade secret, proprietary, or protective-order materials in pending patent applications, reissue applications, and reexamination files before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule for testimony, cross-examination, rebuttal, records and briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed timeline items (A)-(F) and filing schedule: (A) Testimony for petitioner to close (specify approx. 60 days after letter); (B) Time for applicant to file objections to admissibility (approx. 20 days after (A)); (C) Time for petitioner to file supplemental evidence to overcome objections to close (20 days after (B), adjusted for weekends/holidays); (D) Time for applicant to request cross-examination of petitioner’s affiants to close (approx. 20 days after (C)); (E) Time for cross-examination of petitioner’s affiants to close (approx. 30 days after (D)); (F) Rebuttal testimony by applicant to close (approx. 20 days after (E)). One copy of each party's record and exhibits due approx. 30 days after (F); petitioner’s brief due approx. 30 days thereafter; applicant’s brief due approx. 20 days after applicant’s filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify exact calendar dates to avoid confusion; a given period begins with the close of the previous period; early completion does not change closing dates. Applicant and petitioner may agree on a different schedule provided the last brief is due no later than the specified date and a copy of the new schedule is filed. No extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a); petitions to extend must be filed under 37 CFR 1.136(b). All papers must be served in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified deposition transcript filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified transcript of a deposition must be filed in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office within one month after the date of deposition (37 CFR 41.157).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of testimony in public-use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In public use proceedings (whether issue is anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) or obviousness over 35 U.S.C. 103), testimony will be limited to the issues of public use or on sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No testimony will be received on whether the claimed subject matter would have been obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision format and content in public-use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's final decision should be 'analogous [Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences] in an interference proceeding, analyzing the testimony' and stating conclusions; the examiner is not bound by the prior finding that a prima facie case has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner concludes that a public use or sale bar exists, enter a rejection predicating it on the evidence considered and the findings. Even if no rejection is made, the written action should reflect that 35 U.S.C. 102(b) evidence has been considered. Likewise indicate whether a prima facie case (A) has not been established, or (B) has been established and rebutted (see MPEP § 2133.03(e) et seq.). Use of reasons for allowance pursuant to 37 CFR 1.104(e) may be appropriate. There is no review from the examiner's final decision in public use proceedings except by petition under 37 CFR 1.181 for clear error; once application returns to ex parte status, appellate review under 35 U.S.C. 134 and 141-145 may be had.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing normally not held in ex parte and certain inter partes/reissue cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In ex parte cases and in inter partes cases where the pending application is a reissue, an oral hearing is ordinarily not held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose material information (37 CFR 1.56 / 1.555)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material to patentability when it is not cumulative to information already of record or being made of record in the application, and (1) it establishes, by itself or in combination, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes, or is inconsistent with, a position the applicant takes in opposing an argument of unpatentability relied on by the Office or asserting an argument of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is incumbent upon patent applicants and patent owners to bring 'material' information to the attention of the Office, regardless of whether the information is a trade secret, proprietary, or subject to a protective order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a prima facie case of unpatentability
rubrics_metrics.description: A prima facie case of unpatentability is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under the preponderance of the evidence burden-of-proof standard, giving each term in the claim its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, and before any consideration is given to evidence submitted in an attempt to establish a contrary conclusion of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of submitting trade secret, proprietary, and/or protective order materials (MPEP § 724.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information considered trade secret, proprietary, or subject to a protective order must be clearly labeled and filed in a sealed, clearly labeled envelope or container. Each document/item must be labeled 'Trade Secret', 'Proprietary', or 'Subject To Protective Order' and must include complete identifying information for the file, including Office/area to which directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using labels 'Confidential', 'Restricted' or 'Restricted Data' to prevent confusion with national security markings. If 'Subject To Protective Order', include the proceeding/tribunal on each document. The envelope/container must be accompanied by a transmittal letter containing the same identifying information and stating materials are trade secret/proprietary/subject to protective order; a petition under 37 CFR 1.59 and fee to expunge should accompany the envelope/container. Hand-carry to Customer Window or mail to Commissioner for Patents to avoid mishandling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of appropriate envelope/container labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested envelope labels include explicit text such as: 'TRADE SECRET MATERIAL NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC. TO BE OPENED ONLY BY EXAMINER OR OTHER AUTHORIZED U.S. PATENT AND TRADEMARK OFFICE EMPLOYEE. DO NOT SCAN' followed by identifying application information; analogous wording provided for 'PROPRIETARY MATERIAL' and 'MATERIAL SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER' (including tribunal and order details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate changes should be made for papers filed in a reexamination file. Include application number, filing date, title, TC Art Unit, and examiner on labeling and transmittal letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of materials appropriate for submission under MPEP § 724.02
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions contemplated include information 'material to patentability' but do not include information favorable to patentability (e.g., evidence of commercial success).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such favorable information should not be submitted under MPEP § 724.02. If trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials are submitted in amendments, arguments, or affidavits (37 CFR 1.131/1.132), they will be made of record and not given special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office handling on receipt of sealed materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt, the transmittal letter and envelope/container are date stamped, noted on the 'Contents' of the application/reexamination file, and brought to examiner's attention. For Image File Wrapper (IFW) applications, the Office places the envelope/container in an Artifact folder; for paper files the confidential information is retained in the envelope or container.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The face of the file will be annotated to indicate presence of trade secret/proprietary/protective order material and its location. The words 'TRADE SECRET MATERIALS FILED WHICH ARE NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC' are sufficient to indicate presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of materials submitted in applications covered by 35 U.S.C. 122
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under MPEP § 724.02 in an application covered by 35 U.S.C. 122 will be maintained in the original envelope marked 'Not Open To The Public' and will not be publicly available until a determination is made whether the information is important to a reasonable examiner in deciding whether to allow the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(1), materials will be released to the public with other application papers only if no petition to expunge (37 CFR 1.59) was filed prior to mailing of a notice of allowability or notice of abandonment, or a petition was filed and denied. If application is abandoned and a petition to expunge has been filed, the petition will be granted and materials expunged irrespective of importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of materials submitted in reissue applications (37 CFR 1.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under MPEP § 724.02 in a reissue application open to the public under 37 CFR 1.11(b) will be maintained separate from the reissue file and not be publicly available until a determination is made whether the information is important to a reasonable examiner in deciding whether to allow the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reissue application is abandoned and a petition to expunge has been filed, the petition will be granted and materials expunged regardless of importance; if allowed and materials found important, petition denied and materials become permanent part of file and open to public. If no petition filed prior to mailing of notice of allowability, materials become part of file and open to public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of materials submitted in reexamination files (37 CFR 1.11(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under MPEP § 724.02 in a reexamination file open to the public under 37 CFR 1.11(d) will be maintained separate and not publicly available until a determination is made whether the information is important to a reasonable examiner in deciding whether a claim is patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any portion is found important, petition to expunge denied and information becomes permanent part of reexamination file and open to public; if not important, petition granted and information expunged. If no petition filed prior to mailing of a Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC), materials become permanent part of reexamination file and open to public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination standard for expungement (importance to a reasonable examiner)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner or appropriate Office official will determine whether any portion or all of submitted information is important to a reasonable examiner in deciding whether to allow the application to issue as a patent (or whether a claim is patentable in reexamination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information is found important, the petition to expunge will be denied and the materials will become part of the application/reexamination file and available to the public upon issuance; if found not important, the petition will be granted and the information expunged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and timing required for a petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) to expunge materials submitted under MPEP § 724.02
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to expunge information submitted under MPEP § 724.02 must be filed with the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)) and must contain: (A) clear identification of the information to be expunged without disclosure of details; (B) a clear statement that the information is trade secret/proprietary/subject to protective order and not otherwise public; (C) a commitment to retain such information for the period of any patent with regard to which it was submitted; (D) a statement that the petition is submitted by or on behalf of the party in interest who originally submitted the information; (E) the fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition should accompany the submission of the information and be submitted in sufficient time to be acted upon prior to mailing of a notice of allowability or notice of abandonment (or NIRC for reexamination). Timely submission is extremely important; if petition does not accompany initial submission, submit while application/reexamination is pending in the Technology Center and before transmission to the Publishing Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to expunge for unintentionally submitted information
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to expunge information unintentionally submitted in an application (other than original disclosure) may be filed under 37 CFR 1.59(b) provided: (A) the Office can effect return prior to issuance of any patent on the application; (B) it is stated that submission was unintentional and failure to return would cause irreparable harm; (C) information has not otherwise been made public; (D) a commitment to retain such information for the period of any patent with regard to which such information is submitted; (E) it is established to the satisfaction of the Director that the information to be returned is not material under 37 CFR 1.56; (F) the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(g) is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to expunge information that has not been clearly identified as potentially subject to such a request will be treated case-by-case. Applicants are warned that unidentified trade secret/proprietary/protective-order information submitted in an IDS may be placed in an Office prior art search file and may not be retrievable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for papers placed in incorrect application file
rubrics_metrics.description: Where papers were placed in an incorrect application file due to an unintended heading, a petition should request that the papers be expunged rather than transferred to the correct application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office can determine the correct application intended (based on identifying information in the heading), the Office will transfer the papers to the correct file without need of a petition. Grant of a petition to expunge will be governed by factors for unintentional submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of information forming part of the original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to expunge part of the original disclosure must be filed under 37 CFR 1.183 (directed to Office of Petitions) because it requires waiver of 37 CFR 1.59(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must explain why justice requires waiver; such petitions will ordinarily not be favorably entertained. Original disclosures (specification, claims, drawings, preliminary amendment incorporated into oath/declaration) are scanned and changing the USPTO record may not be possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory summary of 37 CFR 1.59 (handling of expungement requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.59 provides that information in an application will not be expunged except as provided in paragraph (b); information forming part of the original disclosure will not be expunged; an applicant may request expungement under paragraph (b) by filing a petition with required fee and establishing to Director's satisfaction that expungement is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expungement of information originally submitted under MPEP § 724.02 or that should have been submitted under § 724.02 is appropriate when petitioner complies with the items in MPEP § 724.05 (I) and the responsible official determines the information is not important to a reasonable examiner. Expungement of inadvertently submitted information is appropriate if conditions are met (see MPEP § 724.05 II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements for public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers in the public use proceeding shall be served in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248.
